decisions.summary: make land returns at once, with refusal and cure, when the claims refusal is an INTRODUCED finding / known drift / anything only an edit or ruling cures
decisions.why: Exactly FR-001 and the approved fix 1 ('stop waiting when the claims gate refuses for a reason waiting can't fix').

decisions.summary: the fast exit fires only when the refusal names NO 'owed (' line, so a refusal carrying an introduced finding AND an owed claim still waits the full round
decisions.why: No in-flight check can cure the introduced part, so the land refuses after the wait anyway: that is FR-001's case literally ('MUST NOT wait ... when the refusal is one no in-flight check can cure') and the GM's 'a reason waiting can't fix'. Not impossible, not implied by the request, and it keeps the 20-minute waste the fix exists to remove. Should say: fail fast whenever any part of the refusal cannot be cured by waiting, listing the owed claims beside the rest.

decisions.summary: an 'owed (' refusal is treated as 'a check may be in flight' and keeps today's wait, because no registry of in-flight claims checks exists
decisions.why: FR-002 and SC-002 key on whether a check IS in flight ('refuses with nothing in flight never enters the claims wait'); the plan substitutes 'the gate says owed', so an owed claim nobody dispatched still waits 20 minutes, a reason waiting can't fix. The stated reason (no registry exists) is an implementation-cost argument, not impossibility: a marker written when a claims check is dispatched/started would make in-flight observable. Should say: wait only while an in-flight check is observable (e.g. such a marker), or take this narrowing to the GM via the arbiter.

decisions.summary: one docstring-blind code id in pipeline/codeid.py (drop module/class/function docstrings and constant-claim strings, dump AST without attributes, hash); gate-stamp calls it; unparsable files hashed by bytes
decisions.why: FR-003/FR-004 and the GM's 'omitting docstrings when hashing code'; one copy of the rule serves the audit.

decisions.summary: gencache._split_sources and render_cache.engine_fingerprint key on codeid
interactive/** (class docstrings are modal text via cls.__doc__) stays hashed by bytes in the roll and render keys, the rule and reason at the point of change
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own words ('failing to strip docstrings when we SHOULD') and carried by FR-004/FR-005's content exception: a docstring that is the artifact's content, hashed blind, would serve a stale render, defeating the cache exactness the request presumes (SC-006). Page assets are not docstrings at all.

decisions.summary: gate-stamp content_id (RAW_AREAS raw), ci/delta engine_key, cohort_known engine_key kept as they are
decisions.why: Already docstring-blind; RAW_AREAS is the existing content exception FR-004 allows.

decisions.summary: ci/state.py tooling_hash moves .py to codeid except each file's MODULE docstring (scripts print it as usage); Makefile and non-.py raw
decisions.why: A content exception under FR-004: a module docstring printed as usage is output the tooling tests can observe. Note, not blocking: the row says today's raw hashing is 'deliberately' so and the plan does not record what that reason was; if the tooling tests read function docstrings too, stripping them serves a stale pass, an FR-004 content case the audit would have missed. Record the reason in research.md and at the point of change.

decisions.summary: ci/gate_config config_hash and record_cache code_sha move .py to codeid; lockfiles/config raw
decisions.why: FR-004: places that fail to strip docstrings when they should, fixed.

decisions.summary: record_build fingerprint kept raw (the built site reads research claims from docstrings); claims fingerprints kept (the claim text is what is checked)
decisions.why: FR-004's own exception: the docstring is content of what the site produces; the GM's 'when we should' implies such sites exist. The claims case is the spec's edge case.

decisions.summary: plan_*, hm_*, record/* other hashes are text, not code: no change
decisions.why: Not code-staleness keys; FR-004 covers code-hashing sites.

decisions.summary: cohort_audit --failed-first/--last-failed/--exitfirst; last run = newest same-block record of this clone, none -> say so and roll all; ordered_specs and roll_until_failure; early stop cancels unstarted, lets started finish, exit 1
decisions.why: FR-007 and the GM's pytest-style modes; letting started seeds finish is pytest-xdist -x behavior in a parallel pool.

decisions.summary: --last-failed/--exitfirst runs write records marked partial, refused by cohort_gate.landing_shaped; cohort-landing passes none of the modes
decisions.why: Enforces FR-008.

decisions.summary: LAST_FAILED reads only the newest record's failing seeds, so failures an EXITFIRST partial run did not roll are forgotten
decisions.why: Full run fails 3, 7, 9; LAST_FAILED=1 EXITFIRST=1 rolls 3, fails, stops - the record says failing {3}; the next LAST_FAILED=1 rolls only 3; once fixed it reports nothing failing, and 7 and 9 reappear only at the landing - the wasted round the GM is cutting. The GM asked for 'the pytest thing'; pytest's lastfailed keeps unrun failures until they pass. Should say: a partial record carries forward the failures of the run it selected from that it did not roll.

decisions.summary: every run prints 'rolled N, served M'
decisions.why: The measurement that enforces SC-001/FR-012; verification of what was asked.

decisions.summary: FR-012 'holds by D3' and is pinned by a test that runs a cohort twice at one code and asserts zero rolled
decisions.why: FR-012 names its test: 'a landing right after a full cohort run at the same code rolls no seed', and the GM's own example is 'run the seeds locally and then do a make landing'. Two cohort runs never exercise the landing path (its worktree, environment and seed block), so 'holds by D3' is a premise the substituted test cannot measure. Should say: the test runs a full cohort, then make cohort-landing (the land path), and asserts zero rolled.

decisions.summary: make probe [WT=] [EXITFIRST=1] runs the landing cohort, HEAD's fresh block and make map for each live hamlet; HEAD's verdicts stored per engine key and block under .git/probe-baselines, rolled once in a detached worktree when absent; EXITFIRST stops at the first seed worse than HEAD's
decisions.why: FR-009, SC-003, SC-004, approved fix 2.

decisions.summary: the probe prints only seeds whose verdict differs from HEAD's
decisions.why: Approved fix 2: 'print each seed's result and each changed field against HEAD'; FR-009: 'per-seed verdict comparisons'. A seed failing the same way at HEAD and in the probe - the seed being iterated on - would be invisible. Should say: print every seed's verdict against HEAD's, differences marked (the field changes may stay changed-only, as the fix's words say).

decisions.summary: task-add writes a section with the alone-off table header and item 6's D35 red exit wording; a SECTION= file whose item 6 lacks make arbiter-ask gets a warning and is filed
decisions.why: FR-010 and approved fix 3.

decisions.summary: Summary, Technical Context (probe-baseline store, reference roll first), Performance bookends, Constitution Check, Project Structure, Complexity Tracking
decisions.why: Restate the spec or lay out the files for decisions above; none decide anything the spec left open beyond them.
